commit.message:
server: add router device memory margin parameter for dynamic unloading (#21231)

* server: add --models-memory-max parameter to allow dynamically unloading models when they exceed a memory size threshold

estimate with to-be-loaded model size included

use no_alloc to get memory requirements for model load

only set model memory_mb if not previously calculated

use memory margin instead of total size limit, apply to each device separately

add server memory debug logging

move llama_context_device_memory function to llama-ext.h

fix model count exceeded check

improve memory_per_device map naming

improve variable naming, fix style

also strip models memory margin from child processes

cont : clean-up

replace device memory map with buft memory map. Use llama_get_memory_breakdown

extract duplicated check into helper function

move model memory estimation to subprocess

precompute name->buft map, map GPU host types to CPU buft

cleanup unused variable

remove duplicated init calls

* adapt to upstream changes

* wip

* common_memory_reports internface

* SERVER_ROLE_MEASURE

* server-models-sched

* fix build

* server : fix memory accounting of measure children and claim spin

A measure child runs no_alloc, so the free memory it reports does not
include its estimate: subtracting self there erased the memory held by
other processes, down to zero with --fit on, and the next load could
overshoot the margin. Subtract self only for instance reports.

A queued load only checked --models-max before claiming, so when the
memory margin blocked it behind a busy model, load() threw and the
waiter retried in a tight loop. Refuse the claim while the limits are
exceeded and no idle model can be unloaded, so the waiter sleeps on
the condition variable until one goes idle.

---------

Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen <son@huggingface.co>
Co-authored-by: Pascal <admin@serveurperso.com>

commit.message:
ui: fix system message row stretching to full prompt height in WebKit (#31246)

The expand button wrapping the system message card defaulted to
inline-block. WebKit takes an inline-block's baseline from its last
line even when that line is clipped by the card's max-height, so the
row grew to the height of the whole prompt and left a large empty gap
below the card. Make the button a block so the row matches the card.

commit.message:
vulkan: fix CI llvmpipe by allowing dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT (#31239)

* vulkan: allow dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT

supports_op rejected every MUL_MAT whose src0 and src1 differ in ne3,
although mul_mm, mul_mmq and mul_mat_vec already broadcast src0 over
dim 3 through broadcast3. Such a matmul then ran on the CPU with a
copy of the weight, and the split layout changed with the number of
streams in the ubatch.

Keep the strict check for MUL_MAT_ID only, and route the broadcast
cases away from mul_mat_vec_nc, the one path that requires equal ne3.

* tests : harden MUL_MAT with permuted dim 3 broadcast cases

Harden the MUL_MAT coverage with a weight broadcast over dim 3 against
a permuted per-stream activation, the shape of an MLA output
projection with a non unified KV cache, for a single token, several
heads and several tokens per stream.

commit.message:
tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving (#31145)

* tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving

Refactor save_models to create only the model, not a llama_context,
which is not needed for saving. Replace the slow std::normal_distribution
draw with a splitmix64 + box-muller normal generator.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

* tests : use a shared pool of normal draws for tensor data

Generate a pool of normal draws once with std::mt19937 and
std::normal_distribution, then have every tensor copy a cyclic slice of
it instead of running a per-tensor box-muller. The name-keyed slice
selection keeps the draw deterministic.

commit.message:
llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape (#31243)

* llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape

qwen4exp (QSA) and glm5-next pick cache cells by index and no longer read the kq_mask values, but they still shaped the selection like the dense kq_mask. Build the selection as [n_kv, n_tokens] over the cache cells instead, and split it into the streams of the K view right before the attention.

This lets the dense mask change its layout (e.g. per-sequence row lists) without touching the sparse layers.

* improve comment

Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov <ggerganov@gmail.com>

* llama : drop the unused build_fused_top_k_mask args, review nits

commit.message:
tests: fix CI riscv timeout in test-llama-context (#31265)

In --models mode the thread count per model is computed and printed,
but never set in the params, so every context runs on the common
default, the number of physical cores. With several models in
parallel this oversubscribes the CPU, and the busy-wait barriers of
the CPU backend make it collapse.

Set the count in cpuparams and cpuparams_batch.

commit.message:
server: expose the reasoning effort levels of the chat template (#31271)

* server: expose the reasoning effort levels of the chat template

The capability probe renders a user turn for each candidate level
(minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and for an unknown level. A
level is honored when it renders without raising and differently from
the unknown level, which shows the template fallback. Levels sharing a
render are aliases and the highest one is kept.

The caps serialize to JSON, and chat_template_caps in /props reports
the list as reasoning_effort_levels, from lowest to highest.

* jinja: keep the caps free of the json dependency

The caps keep reporting their flags as a map, and the effort levels
stay a plain member. common_chat_templates_get_caps() builds the JSON
the server reports from both, so jinja depends on json only for the
probe inputs.

commit.message:
ui: build the reasoning menu from the template effort levels (#31273)

* ui: build the reasoning menu from the template effort levels

When the chat template reports effort levels, the menu offers Default,
Off and those levels, and a pick is sent as reasoning_effort. A
template that reports none keeps the token budget menu.

Picking a model other than the one that produced the last answer resets
the conversation effort to Default, and an effort the current menu
lacks resolves to Default.

* ui: wait for a cold router model before building the request

A router serves the props of a loaded model only, so a request sent to
a cold model was built without its template effort levels and fell
back to a token budget. The request now waits for the model to load,
joining a load already in flight, and a stop during the wait sends
nothing.

Status waiters hold a list per model so a load and the requests that
wait on it each get theirs, and a props request in flight is shared
with a second caller instead of answering null.

commit.message:
sycl: work-group argmax for short TOP_K rows (#31110)

* sycl: work-group argmax for short TOP_K rows

Used angelX to optimize SYCL/drama 3 coordination, results are as follows

Rows with ncols <= max work-group size: one work-item per column, k rounds of work-group argmax. Ties take the lower column, NaN is never picked. Longer rows keep the existing paths.

Arc Pro B70, oneAPI 2026.1, test-backend-ops perf (existing short-row cases), base 9b56ccf00 vs patch, median ratio of 6 rotating A/B/A rounds:

| ncols | nrows | k | base us | patch us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 1024 | 1 | 19.97 | 2.88 | 6.95x |
| 16 | 1024 | 2 | 23.83 | 2.90 | 8.25x |
| 16 | 1024 | 8 | 66.12 | 4.66 | 14.21x |
| 16 | 8192 | 1 | 110.42 | 5.96 | 18.51x |
| 16 | 8192 | 2 | 130.21 | 8.82 | 14.77x |
| 16 | 8192 | 8 | 420.62 | 27.27 | 15.42x |
| 128 | 1024 | 1 | 20.49 | 2.94 | 6.97x |
| 128 | 1024 | 2 | 25.89 | 3.45 | 7.52x |
| 128 | 1024 | 8 | 101.67 | 8.95 | 11.36x |
| 128 | 8192 | 1 | 112.19 | 13.29 | 8.44x |
| 128 | 8192 | 2 | 141.18 | 20.60 | 6.85x |
| 128 | 8192 | 8 | 643.21 | 67.60 | 9.51x |
| 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 17.32 | 14.98 | 1.16x |
| 1024 | 1024 | 2 | 28.77 | 24.02 | 1.20x |
| 1024 | 1024 | 8 | 151.87 | 77.88 | 1.95x |
| 1024 | 8192 | 1 | 156.49 | 138.78 | 1.13x |
| 1024 | 8192 | 2 | 201.47 | 209.18 | 0.96x |
| 1024 | 8192 | 8 | 1006.25 | 632.60 | 1.59x |

The 1024 x 8192, k=2 case is 3.7% slower.

Correctness: test-backend-ops -o TOP_K 533/533 and -o ARGSORT 98/98 on the patch, again on the rebase onto 3f03b1772.

Full test-backend-ops aborts on base and patch alike at the non-F32 SWIGLU_OAI assert (element_wise.cpp:1187, see #30857). With only those cases excluded: 20145/20173 on base and patch. One CPY f16->q2_0 [256,2,3,4] failure was seen once on the patch, and 3/3 re-runs pass on base and patch. All other patch-run failures also fail on base.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* made changes as suggested

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

commit.message:
common, mtmd: bound control vector layer indices and M-RoPE position loops (#31336)

* common: bound control vector layer indices by the model layer count

A direction tensor layer index is parsed from the tensor name with no
upper bound, and the buffer size and write offset are computed in int.
A large index overflows both, so the accumulation writes before the
start of the buffer.

Pass the model layer count to the loader, reject indices above it like
the existing zero index check, and compute the sizes in size_t.

* mtmd: fill M-RoPE positions by whole merge tiles

The position loops of the Qwen-VL, GLM, PaddleOCR and Qwen2.5-VL
encoders hardcode a 2x2 merge inside a stride of n_merge, so a patch
grid that is not a multiple of the merge writes past the positions
buffer. Iterate over whole merge tiles with n_merge inner steps, which
bounds the writes by the patch count and gives the same positions on
aligned grids.

PaddleOCR also requires a merge aligned image at graph build, as the
Qwen-VL family already does.

commit.message:
tests: fix CI flakes in server cancel and sleep tests (#31330)

test_cancel_request enables context shift so the generation only ends
when the request is cancelled, then polls /slots with a deadline.
Without context shift the generation fills the context and frees the
slot on its own on fast machines, so the test passes even with
cancellation disabled.

test_server_sleep uses the existing wait_for_sleep helper instead of a
fixed sleep.

commit.message:
ggml-openvino: slice view inputs of SCALE (#31334)

SCALE now accepts a src0 view with arbitrary row strides. translate_scale
used the raw input, and on the dynamic path a VIEW translates to its whole
source tensor, so a strided view input scaled the entire source. The model
output then had the source's size, and copying it back overran the result
buffer, which crashes test-backend-ops on the SCALE view cases.

Slice the input with process_view_input_new, as the other translators do.
Reject an in-place SCALE on a non-contiguous view: its result is copied
back densely and would land in the wrong elements.

commit.message:
sycl : vectorize reordered-layout dequantization stores (Q4_0, K-quants, IQ3, MXFP4) (#30976)

* sycl : widen reordered q4_0 dequantization stores

The reordered-layout Q4_0 conversion kernel processed one qs byte per
work-item with two scalar stores, strided 16 elements apart. Give it
the same treatment the Q8_0 kernel got in #30775: a flat
sycl::range<1> launch with four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item
inside one 32-element block and two vec<dst_t,4> stores.

Same float math and rounding as the scalar kernel; output is
bit-identical. The existing k % QK4_0 == 0 assert guarantees whole
32-element blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The
now-unreferenced scalar reorder kernel is removed.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a
reorder-installed tensor): +6.4% to +7.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_0
models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill and decode
unchanged; PPL within run noise.

* sycl : vectorize reordered q4_K dequantization stores

The reordered-layout Q4_K conversion kernel already loads its
quantized inputs through sycl::vec but writes the dequantized
results with scalar stores. Build the results in a vec<dst_t,n>
register and emit two vector stores instead. Same per-element
math; output is bit-identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a
reorder-installed tensor): +14.7% to +15.3% pp512/pp2048 on
Q4_K-dominant models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout
prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : remap reordered q5_K dequantization to vec4 loads/stores

The reordered-layout Q5_K conversion kernel gave each thread only
four outputs fed by scalar ql/qh byte loads plus a local-memory
scale broadcast, so the stores were never its bottleneck: widening
the stores alone measured within noise on mixed-quant models and
+0.5% on a q5_K-dominant model. Re-decompose to 32 threads per
block, each consuming four consecutive ql and qh bytes and emitting
two aligned vec<dst_t,4> stores; a 4-element run shares one scale
pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill on a q5_K-dominant 27B model: +3.6%
pp512/pp2048 over the scalar kernel; fresh-layout prefill, decode
and PPL unchanged. The GET_ROWS reorder path moves to the same
32-thread decomposition.

* sycl : remap reordered q6_K dequantization to vec4 stores

The reordered-layout Q6_K conversion kernel wrote four scalars per
thread, strided 32 elements apart, each pair of neighbors sharing
neither instruction stream nor store transaction. Re-decompose the
same 64-thread work-group so each thread emits one aligned
vec<dst_t,4>: a 4-element run shares one 16-element scale group,
one ql nibble source and one qh bit pair, so the per-element math
and the output are identical to the scalar kernel.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +28.7% pp512/pp2048 on a Q6_K 27B
model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : vectorize reordered q3_K dequantization stores

Each thread of the reordered-layout Q3_K conversion kernel already
computes four consecutive outputs; build them in a vec<dst_t,4>
register and emit one vector store instead of four scalars. Same
per-element math; output is bit-identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +16.8% pp512/pp2048 on a Q3_K-dominant
27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : vectorize reordered iq3_xxs/iq3_s dequantization stores

Both reordered-layout IQ3 conversion kernels write eight contiguous
outputs per thread as scalar stores (four from each grid lookup).
Build two vec<dst_t,4> registers and emit two vector stores. Same
per-element math; output is bit-identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +20.3% to +21.1% pp512/pp2048 on
IQ3_XXS- and IQ3_S-dominant 27B models; fresh-layout prefill,
decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : remap reordered q2_K dequantization to vec4 stores

Re-decompose the reordered-layout Q2_K conversion kernel the same
way as Q6_K: one aligned vec<dst_t,4> per thread instead of four
scalars strided 32 apart. A 4-element run shares one scale byte and
one 2-bit lane, so the per-element math and the output are
identical to the scalar kernel.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +13.1% pp512/pp2048 on a Q2_K-dominant
27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : widen reordered mxfp4 dequantization stores

Give the reordered-layout MXFP4 conversion kernel the same flat
sycl::range<1> launch as Q4_0: four qs bytes (8 outputs) per
work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec<dst_t,4> stores.
Same LUT lookups and per-block scale; output is bit-identical. The
k % QK_MXFP4 == 0 assert guarantees whole blocks, so the k/8 launch
covers every row exactly. The old scalar kernel is removed.

The reordered layout for MXFP4 is installed on the MoE expert path
(reorder_qw_mxfp4_moe); dense MXFP4 tensors keep the normal layout.

Arc Pro B70, MXFP4 MoE 20B model: +57% pp2048 / +61% pp512 prefill
(primed and fresh alike), decode unchanged, PPL within the model's
run-to-run noise.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill on a q5_K-dominant 27B model: +3.6%
pp512/pp2048 over the scalar kernel; fresh-layout prefill, decode
and PPL unchanged. The GET_ROWS reorder path moves to the same
32-thread decomposition.

* sycl : remap reordered q6_K dequantization to vec4 stores

The reordered-layout Q6_K conversion kernel wrote four scalars per
thread, strided 32 elements apart, each pair of neighbors sharing
neither instruction stream nor store transaction. Re-decompose the
same 64-thread work-group so each thread emits one aligned
vec<dst_t,4>: a 4-element run shares one 16-element scale group,
one ql nibble source and one qh bit pair, so the per-element math
and the output are identical to the scalar kernel.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +28.7% pp512/pp2048 on a Q6_K 27B
model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : vectorize reordered q3_K dequantization stores

Each thread of the reordered-layout Q3_K conversion kernel already
computes four consecutive outputs; build them in a vec<dst_t,4>
register and emit one vector store instead of four scalars. Same
per-element math; output is bit-identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +16.8% pp512/pp2048 on a Q3_K-dominant
27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : vectorize reordered iq3_xxs/iq3_s dequantization stores

Both reordered-layout IQ3 conversion kernels write eight contiguous
outputs per thread as scalar stores (four from each grid lookup).
Build two vec<dst_t,4> registers and emit two vector stores. Same
per-element math; output is bit-identical.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +20.3% to +21.1% pp512/pp2048 on
IQ3_XXS- and IQ3_S-dominant 27B models; fresh-layout prefill,
decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : remap reordered q2_K dequantization to vec4 stores

Re-decompose the reordered-layout Q2_K conversion kernel the same
way as Q6_K: one aligned vec<dst_t,4> per thread instead of four
scalars strided 32 apart. A 4-element run shares one scale byte and
one 2-bit lane, so the per-element math and the output are
identical to the scalar kernel.

Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +13.1% pp512/pp2048 on a Q2_K-dominant
27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged.

* sycl : widen reordered mxfp4 dequantization stores

Give the reordered-layout MXFP4 conversion kernel the same flat
sycl::range<1> launch as Q4_0: four qs bytes (8 outputs) per
work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec<dst_t,4> stores.
Same LUT lookups and per-block scale; output is bit-identical. The
k % QK_MXFP4 == 0 assert guarantees whole blocks, so the k/8 launch
covers every row exactly. The old scalar kernel is removed.

The reordered layout for MXFP4 is installed on the MoE expert path
(reorder_qw_mxfp4_moe); dense MXFP4 tensors keep the normal layout.

Arc Pro B70, MXFP4 MoE 20B model: +57% pp2048 / +61% pp512 prefill
(primed and fresh alike), decode unchanged, PPL within the model's
run-to-run noise.

commit.message:
metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec, full threadgroups for unary/binary/GLU (#31075)

* metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec kernel

Decode the fp4 values with the fp16 bit trick instead of a threadgroup lookup table, and load the packed nibbles as aligned 32-bit words. The kernel no longer uses threadgroup memory.

* metal : launch contiguous unary and binary ops with full threadgroups

The contiguous unary path and the row-broadcast binary path used one thread per threadgroup. Use up to 256 threads per threadgroup and bound-check the tail.

* metal : split GLU rows across threadgroups

A GLU row ran on one threadgroup, so single-row decode used a single threadgroup for the whole op. Split each row over threadgroups of up to 256 threads.

commit.message:
ui: keep chats at the bottom until the reader scrolls up (#31311)

* ui: land at the bottom of a conversation every time it opens

Opening a long conversation often stopped short of its end:

- the press grace counted from page load (pressedAt = 0), so a chat that
  landed within 400 ms of a refresh did not follow the rows realizing
  after the jump
- the click that opened a chat (sidebar row, tab) started the same grace,
  so navigating by click had the same problem
- any scroll event away from the bottom stopped following, including the
  ones the browser fires itself while the chat settles
- the chat screen outlives its routes, so going back to the last landed
  conversation through the new-chat screen skipped the landing entirely

scrollToBottom() now clears the grace, only an upward scroll away from the
bottom stops following, and every navigation lands anew. Navigations into
a chat also disable SvelteKit's scroll reset, which moved the previous
conversation to its top for a few frames.

Where overflow-anchor is supported, a 1px pin after the messages is the
only scroll anchor while following, so the browser keeps the bottom in
place itself; WebKit keeps the resize observer.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: let nested agentic content scrollers chain to the chat

Reasoning, shell output and code blocks used overscroll-behavior:
contain, so the wheel stopped dead at their edges instead of
scrolling the conversation.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: stop following the stream as soon as the reader scrolls up

A trackpad or smooth wheel scrolls in steps smaller than the at-bottom
threshold, so each step up was re-stuck and snapped back on the next
growth while a response streamed. Any upward move that is not content
shrinking now releases at once.

The attach effect also read the hook's own state, so every flip
re-attached and re-measured, which undid such a release.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

a chat also disable SvelteKit's scroll reset, which moved the previous
conversation to its top for a few frames.

Where overflow-anchor is supported, a 1px pin after the messages is the
only scroll anchor while following, so the browser keeps the bottom in
place itself; WebKit keeps the resize observer.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: let nested agentic content scrollers chain to the chat

Reasoning, shell output and code blocks used overscroll-behavior:
contain, so the wheel stopped dead at their edges instead of
scrolling the conversation.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: stop following the stream as soon as the reader scrolls up

A trackpad or smooth wheel scrolls in steps smaller than the at-bottom
threshold, so each step up was re-stuck and snapped back on the next
growth while a response streamed. Any upward move that is not content
shrinking now releases at once.

The attach effect also read the hook's own state, so every flip
re-attached and re-measured, which undid such a release.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

commit.message:
memory: refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch (#31368)

* memory: refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch

The recurrent memory and the DSV4 cache accepted any rollback up to
n_rs_seq, whether or not the last ubatch wrote that snapshot. Each now
records the deepest rollback its last ubatch guarantees and seq_rm
refuses anything past it:

- recurrent: n - 1 for a ubatch of n <= n_rs_seq + 1 tokens, 0 for a
  longer one, which only guarantees the final state
- DSV4: min(n, n_rs_seq), the snapshots are rebuilt from the state
  before the ubatch

The dead rollback block of the rollback test becomes the assertion it
asked for, and rollback_bound checks the exact bound of each memory
after ubatches of 1, 2, n_rs_seq + 1 and n_rs_seq + 2 tokens.

* tests: address review from ggerganov

Detect architectures with llama_arch_from_string in comp_padding and
arch_reserves_single_seq, as in rollback_bound.

output share a buffer type (CPU-only, -ngl 0) held the table twice:

commit.message:
hexagon : fix DMA transfers with strides > 24 bits (#31442)

* hexagon : fix DMA transfers with strides > 24 bits

On v75+ the 2D DMA descriptor stores row_size and strides in 24 bits.
dma_queue_push sent oversized strides to fallback_2d, which only splits
nrows, so strides of 16 MB or more were truncated - wrong addresses.
Fix will fall back to one transfer per row in that case.

Also added two CONT tests with source strides over 16 MB.

* hex-dma: refactor the fallback paths to remove duplication

commit.message:
webgpu : fix CI by keeping scratch alloc sizes monotonic in batch length (#31422)

* webgpu: keep scratch alloc sizes monotonic in the batch length

The flash attention vec path and the MMVQ path append a scratch area
after dst, but get_alloc_size only accounted for it when the current
batch takes that path. The size was therefore not monotonic in the
batch length: a graph reserved at n_ubatch (tiled path, no scratch)
or at one token did not cover batches of 2 to 19 query rows, and
GGML_SCHED_NO_REALLOC builds aborted on an unexpected reallocation.

Pass the row count to both path predicates and size the scratch with
the row count clamped to the longest batch the short path serves.

* nit: align the mmvq pipeline key with clang-format 22

* webgpu: address review @yomaytk, name the mat-vec row threshold

* ui: show interrupted state for tool calls that never returned

The chat-level streaming flag was applied to every assistant message, so a
tool call left without a result in an earlier message kept spinning while a
newer reply streamed. Scope streaming to the last assistant message and mark
finished calls without a result as interrupted.

commit.message:
ui: keep queued steering messages in their own conversation (#31304)

A message queued while a conversation was busy was re-sent through
sendMessage, which targets the active conversation, so switching chats
before the turn ended delivered it into the wrong one. Re-send only when
the owning conversation is active; otherwise keep it queued there and
flush it when that conversation is opened again.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

commit.message:
vulkan: add tensor-parallel allreduce function (#25051)

* vulkan: add tensor-parallel all-reduce communication

* vulkan: require shared semaphores for tensor communication

Assisted-by: Codex

* vulkan: reduce directly from shared host buffers

Assisted-by: Codex

* vulkan: fix ring all-reduce races with 3+ devices

Two hazards in the tensor-parallel ring all-reduce made -sm tensor output
non-deterministic with three GPUs:

- With n = 3, step t's host-slot region starts at t * cels * 2 bytes, which
  is not a multiple of 32, so consecutive steps' transfer copies share a
  32-byte sector of the imported host memory. On NVIDIA the later copy's
  leading bytes (up to 10 F16 values at the start of every chunk) end up
  stale in host memory, even when the copies are ordered by a semaphore.
  Give every step its own 256-byte-aligned region. n = 2 and n = 4 already
  had aligned regions for the usual sizes, so their layout is unchanged.

- A single-shot all-reduce leaves every device's host slot being read by all
  peers, but the next ring round only ordered its first transfer after nextd,
  and only from round 2 on. With n >= 3 a device could overwrite its slot
  while prevd was still summing it. Wait for all peers on the first ring
  round after a single-shot all-reduce.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* vulkan: fold the tensor-parallel all-reduce into the compute submissions

With -sm tensor the meta backend drives every device from one thread and calls
graph_compute once per subgraph (two per layer), so decode was bound by the CPU
cost of submitting, not by the GPUs: ~1500 vkQueueSubmit per token for a 64-layer
model on two GPUs, with the GPUs idle ~40% of the time.

- Don't split subgraphs by flops while a communicator is active. The heuristic
  was tuned for whole graphs and turned each small subgraph into ~5 submits.
- Fold the small (single-shot) all-reduce into the compute submissions: the
  last command buffer of a subgraph stays open, the all-reduce appends the
  gather copy to it and submits it, then opens the next command buffer with the
  peer waits and the reduce, which the next subgraph is recorded into. Each
  subgraph now costs one submit per device. The reserved progress value is
  attached by whichever path submits the open context.
- Alternate between two host slots, placed outside the ring's regions, so the
  gather no longer needs a WAR wait on the peers' previous reduce.
- On synchronize, submit the deferred work of every device in the group first,
  so the tail of the graph runs on all devices in parallel.
- Wait for the transfer queue as well as the compute queue before freeing or
  reallocating communication buffers, and don't leave a stale cap behind when a
  reallocation fails.

qwen3.5 27B Q8_0 on RTX 4090s, tg128: 2 GPUs 32.2 -> 49.7 t/s, 3 GPUs 20.9 ->
40.0, 4 GPUs 15.0 -> 27.6; pp512 on 2 GPUs 2138 -> 2320. Greedy output is
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* - Two-phase all-reduce over shared host memory: write own slot + signal, wait peers + add from their slots
- One exported timeline per device, no backend hooks; comm work recorded in the backend compute ctx
- F16 wire above 1 MiB, F32 below; small reductions ride with the next graph submit
- Double-buffered, grow-only host slots; zero-size splits zeroed
- Remove ring, transfer-queue leg, device staging, shrink, Windows shims
- comm_init returns nullptr when unsupported; add GGML_VK_COMM_DISABLE
- No flops-based submit splitting for graphs below 1 GFLOP

[rebased onto the ring all-reduce fix and the folded all-reduce, which this design replaces; their backend hooks are removed here]

* add minimal submit split size

* replace opaque_fd with sync_fd for spec compliance

* add precision check

* add semaphore pool

* rename env var, add logging if requirements not met

* reduce comments

* code improvements

* vulkan: use posix_memalign for the tensor-parallel host buffers

std::aligned_alloc is unavailable on Android bionic below API 28, which
upstream switched away from in #30828; do the same for the communicator's
host slots.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* vulkan: synchronize the tensor-parallel all-reduce through the host

Exchanging SYNC_FD semaphores costs a kernel wake-up on every all-reduce:
on NVIDIA the waiting GPU starts ~35 us after its peer has finished, which
is most of the idle time in a decode step. OPAQUE_FD semaphores avoid that
but must not be imported into another physical device.

Use only device-local timeline semaphores instead. Each device signals
done[i] once its partial sum is in host memory (after a barrier that makes
it available to the host), and a bridge thread signals go[i] from the host
once all peers of i are done. The waiting side makes the host memory
visible with a host-write barrier, since its submit predates the data.
The thread spins for up to 200 us on each wait (GGML_VK_ALLREDUCE_SPIN_US)
and then blocks, so it is idle when there is no work. This also takes the
per-round fd export, dup and import calls off the main thread and drops the
VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd requirement and the binary semaphore pool.

Graphs below 1 GFLOP, such as tensor-parallel decode slices, are no longer
split into several submits.

qwen3.5 27B Q8_0 on RTX 4090s, tg128: 2 GPUs 37.2 -> 45.4 t/s, 3 GPUs
24.1 -> 35.5, 4 GPUs 16.5 -> 27.1; pp512 unchanged. Greedy output is
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* use sync_fd on mesa drivers

* refactor for readability

* move sync_fd semaphore handling to thread, trigger mesa submit threads

* move allreduce functions to new cpp file

* clean comments

* smaller fixes, code improvements

---------

Co-authored-by: Ruben Ortlam <rortlam@redhat.com>

commit.message:
docs: CANN backend supports BF16 on 910B, document GGML_CANN_NO_PINNED (#31249)

The note under 'Run the inference' still said that the CANN backend only
supports FP16/Q4_0/Q8_0 models, while the DataType table in the same file,
and ggml-cann.cpp (BF16 is enabled for MUL_MAT, GET_ROWS, CPY and CONT for
every non-310P device), say otherwise. Spell out the per-device support and
mark BF16 as unsupported on 310P instead of leaving the cell empty.

GGML_CANN_NO_PINNED is read by ggml-cann.cpp when allocating host buffers
and when advertising the host_buffer device capability, but it was not
documented, so the escape hatch for a failing pinned host allocation was
not discoverable.

commit.message:
llama : flash_attn_ext_rows - more efficient unified kv for multi-seq (#29510)

* llama : use llm_attn_mask and kv_rows for unified attention

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov <ggerganov@gmail.com>

* cont : optimize `get_seq_cells`

* llama : build the kv_rows lists from per-sequence cell bitmaps

Keep a bitmap over the cells for each sequence (the transpose of `seq`), updated in seq_pos_inc/dec, and build the cell lists by walking its set bits. The lists stay in cell order, cells shared by several sequences go to every list, and nothing has to be rebuilt when cells are removed.

Also leave out of the lists the cells that the SWA hides from every token of the slice (standard and chunked SWA).

* cont : make get_kv_rows_p_min private

* cont : minor metal

* llama : use kv_rows for every ubatch of a unified cache

A ubatch made of equal-length runs with a single sequence each (f.ex. the drafts of several slots) now splits into per-sequence slices.

Any other ubatch (interleaved, uneven or coupled sequences) becomes a single slice over the cells of all its sequences instead of falling back to the dense KQ mask, so the graph keeps the topology of the reserved graph.

* llama : merge get_kv_rows_seq_ids and get_kv_rows_p_min into get_kv_rows_slices

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

---------

Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov <ggerganov@gmail.com>

commit.message:
mtmd: Pocket tts - support for voices without voice cloning (#31429)

* feat: support PocketTTS voices with no voice cloning

The kyutai/pocket-tts-without-voice-cloning weights ship predefined voices as the
backbone KV state after the voice prompt. The converter turns each state back into
the prompt embeddings and stores them in the mmproj (voice.<name>), the zeroed voice
encoder is left out, and the "voice" field of /tts and --tts-voice select one of them.
A speaker reference is rejected when the model has no voice encoder.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* convert : pocket-tts voices never fail the conversion, log the drift of the state

The voice states shipped by Kyutai are not always the ones the pack's
weights give for the prompt: italian, german and spanish match within the
bf16 rounding, english_2026-04 is 2% off and french 20% (its layer 0 state
comes from other weights), while the reference loads them as is and they
still sound like the same voice. The converter now re-prompts the backbone
with the recovered embeddings, compares the whole state and logs the
distance per voice, warning above 5%. A state that does not belong to the
weights at all is skipped, so the packs of kyutai/pocket-tts convert too.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* mtmd : list the predefined voices, expose them in GET /props

mtmd_gen_audio_info gains n_voices and mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name() the
names, with the voices worded as a feature of any audio generation model.
The server lists them under "voices" in /props when the model ships some.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* server : an unknown voice is a bad request

A model with predefined voices answers 400 naming the voice instead of 500
"failed to process TTS prompt". A model without them ignores "voice" with a
warning, as the other audio generation models do.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* refactor api

* fix conversion

* small renaming

* fix lint

* tts : a model with predefined voices speaks with the first one by default

Without a voice prompt such a model only produces near silence. When neither
a voice nor a speaker reference is given, llama-tts and the server now take
the first predefined voice and say so in the log, as the LFM3-Audio template
does with its default voice.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* mtmd : one comment per voice accessor, converter states the rule only

The clip.h comment described clip_gen_get_voice but sat above all three
functions; the converter comment quoted the drift measured per pack, which
goes stale with the next upload of the weights.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* clean up redundant code and comments

* mtmd: match the LFM3-Audio voice name case-insensitively

The tts chat template lowers the voice name, so Male speaks with
the male voice; the voice lookup lowers it the same way and names the
bitmap after the canonical voice.

---------

Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen <son@huggingface.co>
Co-authored-by: Pascal <admin@serveurperso.com>

commit.message:
hexagon: tiled hvx permute (#31446)

* hexagon: add tiled HVX transpose path for permuted CONT/CPY

Permuted copies where dst dim 0 is strided in src, but some other src dim
is contiguous, used to fall back to HTP_COPY_KERNEL_RESHAPE. That issues
one DMA descriptor per element. The channel-first <-> channel-last
permutes around per-channel norms (e.g. [W,H,T,C] <-> [C,W,H,T] in video
VAEs) ht this path, and these copies ran at about 45 MB/s.

Add HTP_COPY_KERNEL_TRANSPOSE for same-type, same-shape f32/f16 copies
into a contiguous dst.

Host:
  - drop extent-1 dims and merge dims that stay adjacent in src into a
    canonical view, stored in the kernel params. There are no minimum
    size limits.
  - the copy is treated as a 2D transpose between dst dim 0 and the
    contiguous src dim, batched over the remaining dims.
  - tiles are sized to 64 KB per buffer and halved until they fit in
    session VTCM. blkk is capped so the halfword vgather offsets fit in
    16 bits.

Kernel, per tile:
  - 2D DMA of blk0 strided src rows (blkk contiguous elements each)
    into VTCM
  - vgather transpose in 32x32 (f32) or 64x64 (f16) blocks
  - 2D DMA of blkk contiguous rows out to dst

Staged and transposed buffers are double-buffered, so the next tile's
input DMA overlaps the current transpose and output DMA. Tiles are split
across threads and mdev sessions.

Small dims:
  - packed mode: when dim k follows dim 0 and dim 0 divides the HVX
    lanes (f32: 2/4/8/16, f16: 2/4/.../32), one vgather writes several
    whole dst rows, and each tile goes out as one contiguous DMA.
  - when the contiguous src dim fits in one vector, it is staged exactly
    and the tile is made long along dim 0.

All other copies select the same kernels as before.

Tests: add test_cont cases for perms {1,2,3,0} and {3,0,1,2}, f32 and
f16, at various sizes.

* hexagon: cpy transpose cleanups

- fix vgather halfword offset comments: offsets are unsigned 16-bit, caps are kept lower for speed
- set packed directly in the packed case
- add dim_k == 3 CONT tests (full reversal)

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* hexagon: use cpy transpose path for ne[0] == 1 permutes

- drop the nb[0] check in the transpose solver: size-1 dims are skipped, and the canonical tp.nb[0] check covers packed dim 0
- try the transpose path before SAMESHAPE_SAMETYPE, which did one DMA per element for these
- add ne[0] == 1 permute CPY tests

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* hex-cpy: further improve cpy

Bring in improvements from aizip branch/PR.

Cleanup kparams and replace divs with fastdiv.

Co-authored-by: Yiwei Shao <yiwei@aizip.ai>

* hex-cpy: avoid vtcm bank conflicts

* hex-cpy: trim down the comments

* cpy-test: trim down new tests that cover permute scenarios

---------

Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky <maxk@qti.qualcomm.com>
Co-authored-by: Yiwei Shao <yiwei@aizip.ai>

commit.message:
kv-cache : never return 0 kv_rows for sequences without cells (#31570)

A cache that shares the cells of another one (f.ex. the gemma4 assistant) can build a graph before its sequences have any cells, f.ex. at the server warmup. get_n_kv_rows() then returned 0, which means that kv_rows are not used, so the graph fell back to the dense KQ mask and the scheduler re-planned for it. Later graphs with larger masks then aborted with GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1.

On the non-OCP path, ue4m3_fp32_lut has 128 entries and is indexed with the raw scale byte. ggml_validate_row_data accepts every byte and ggml_ue4m3_to_fp32 ignores bit 7, so a byte >= 0x80 reads past the shared array. Vulkan robustness does not cover shared memory.

Size the table, both init loops, and the two host shared-memory budgets to 256 entries. ue4m3_to_fp32_build() already masks the exponent and treats only 0 and 0x7F as special, so entries 128-255 match the CPU. A 256-entry table keeps 0xFF distinct from 0x7F: the CPU decodes 0xFF as a non-zero value and 0x7F as zero.

Each NVFP4 pipeline uses 512 more bytes of shared memory. ggml_fp32_to_ue4m3 never sets bit 7, so models quantized by llama.cpp are unaffected.

commit.message:
vulkan: skip maxStorageBufferRange pre-check for non-compute tensors (#31114)

* vulkan: skip maxStorageBufferRange pre-check for non-compute tensors

Pre-allocated leaf tensors and views (GGML_OP_NONE / GGML_OP_VIEW) are never
executed by the backend, but were still rejected by the descriptor-size
pre-check in ggml_backend_vk_device_supports_op when larger than
maxStorageBufferRange on devices without shader_64b_indexing. The scheduler
then aborts with 'pre-allocated tensor (...) in a buffer (Vulkan0) that cannot
run the operation (NONE)' - e.g. the MoE expert cache banks (llama-moe-cache)
of a 256-expert model with --moe-cache-mib on GCN GPUs, where a whole bank
(2.4 GB) exceeds the limit while the consuming ops only access small
per-step views.

Skip the size pre-check for non-compute ops (NONE and VIEW); the buffer type
allocation limit still bounds the actual allocation, and compute ops keep
validating their sources.

Tested on AMD Radeon Pro VII (gfx906, no shader_64b_indexing):
- before: GGML_ABORT 'pre-allocated tensor (moe_cache.0.blk.0.ffn_down_exps.weight) ... cannot run the operation (NONE)' with llama-cli -ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 6144 (Cyber-Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B, qwen35moe, 256 experts per layer)
- after: loads and generates at 8.1 t/s (vs 0.6 t/s without the cache)
- regression: -ncmoe 16 path unchanged (19.2 t/s), qwen3moe/qwen35moe without cache unchanged

Fixes #30697

* vulkan: use ggml_op_is_empty for the non-compute size-check skip

---------

commit.message:
meta: support GLM-5.3 next sm tensor (#30499)

* meta: support GLM-5.3 next sm tensor

* glm5-next : cont q_absorbed for -sm tensor with non-unified KV

* meta : keep GGML_OP_ARANGE in ggml.h order

* glm5-next : split MLA heads in pairs for -sm tensor

The MLA cache has a single KV head, so the heads on a device are its GQA
ratio. The HIP tile FA kernel for D=512 needs an even GQA ratio; with 3
devices the 16 heads of the test model were split 5/5/6 and it aborted.

* meta : keep the split for views inside one slab of the split axis

With a non-unified KV cache, build_attn_mha splits q into streams with a
view. For a permuted q, e.g. the absorbed query of glm5-next, that view
aborted with "view of permuted tensor not implemented". The split is now
kept if every other dim of the source and the view stays inside one slab
of the split axis. The per-device strides are only rescaled above it.

From tetherto/qvac-fabric-llm.cpp#353.

Co-authored-by: Pratik Narola <pratik.narola@tether.io>

* glm5-next : drop the q_absorbed cont

The meta backend can now split the per-stream view of the permuted q, so
the cont is not needed for -sm tensor with a non-unified KV cache. With
the cont, the q of flash attention was not contiguous, and when FA ran on
the CPU (WebGPU) the meta get_tensor aborted.

---------

Co-authored-by: Pratik Narola <pratik.narola@tether.io>

commit.message:
conversion : use original model tensor names in _flush_nvfp4_experts (#31427)

This commit updates the _flush_nvfp4_experts to take a new parameter
which is a dictionary mapping the key to the original model tensor name.

The motivation for this is that I noticed that the tensor names being
looked up were not the original model tensor names, for example:
```console
  model.layers.1.mlp.experts.up_proj.weight
```
But _nvfp4_layer_algo uses the original per-expert names:
```console
(Pdb) p self._nvfp4_layer_algo
{
'backbone.layers.1.mixer.experts.0.up_proj': 'W4A16_NVFP4',
...
```
This means that the lookup will never match for experts and fall back to
_nvfp4_global_algo. If the global algo is W4A16_NVFP4 then this would
go unnoticed, but for a model like
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 which is
MIXED_PRECISION, the expert tensors will not get prec_a4=false so they
would use the native W4A4 path on Blackwell even though the original
model tensors declare them as W4A16_NVFP4.

commit.message:
ui: add Playwright harness for recording demo videos (#31318)

* ui: add Playwright harness for recording demo videos

Scripted walkthroughs under tools/ui/demo are recorded with Playwright and
exported as H.264 mp4 for pull requests (demo/pr) and docs (demo/docs).
Fixture MCP servers and seeded settings keep recordings deterministic, a
drawn cursor and captions make the flow readable, and DEMO_UI_DIR points
the recording at another checkout such as a PR worktree.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: record demo scripts from PR descriptions and a configurable storage

Demo scripts no longer live in the repo. `npm run demo:pr -- <number>`
records the `ts demo` block from a PR description against the PR head,
uploads the mp4, a GIF preview and the script to DEMO_STORAGE, and links
the preview in a `## Demo` section of the PR description.
`npm run demo:docs` records the docs scripts kept in DEMO_STORAGE.
DEMO_STORAGE (hf:// buckets or file://) and the public URL are read
from tools/ui/.env.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: import generated conversations into demo recordings

Demos can now start with existing chats: `test.use({ traces })` imports
llama.app JSONL traces through Settings > Import/Export before the video
starts. Built-in traces are generated deterministically, other names are
downloaded from DEMO_TRACES_DATASET, and `demo:traces` pushes the built-in
ones there. Adds `demo.scroll` for wheel scrolling.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: keep demo captions clear of the chat form and isolate concurrent runs

Captions move to the top of the frame, since at the bottom they covered
the chat form a demo is often about. Each recording run gets its own
Playwright output folder, so a run starting elsewhere no longer clears
another run's video before it is saved.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: record demos at 2x and 60 fps with human-like timing

Recording goes through Chromium's screencast instead of Playwright's
video, which encoded VP8 at about 1 Mbit/s at 1x. Frames are captured at
the device pixel ratio (DEMO_SCALE, default 2) and encoded into a 60 fps
H.264 mp4, starting once the page has settled.

The cursor now glides faster along a slight arc with Fitts-like
durations, settles briefly before each click, and typing and pauses vary
a little. The randomness is seeded per demo, so re-recording gives the
same motion.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: document the demo harness prerequisites

The demo README now lists the tools the harness needs and what each is
for, and walks through creating the Hugging Face bucket and the optional
traces dataset, with the matching .env settings.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: version linked demo URLs so re-recorded previews refresh

GitHub's image proxy caches a preview by URL, so a demo re-recorded at
the same PR head kept showing the old GIF. The Demo section now links
the files with a content hash in the query string.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: label PRs that feature a video demo

Adds a `video demo` label and a workflow that applies it when a PR
description has a demo written by the UI demo pipeline (the managed
demo:start/demo:end markers, or a preview linking to a demo video),
and removes it when that section is gone.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ci: label video demos with gh instead of github-script

The label workflow now runs the gh CLI in a shell step, like
pr-draft-label.yml, so it needs no action outside the repository's
allowed list. The video link check only counts videos uploaded for the
PR itself, so a description linking other PRs' demos isn't labeled.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: zoom demos in on details with a two-finger pinch

demo.zoom pinches in on a control or a point, holds, and pinches back out
to 1x, so a detail too small to read in the frame can be shown up close.
It drives Chromium's own pinch gesture, so the page's fixed bars stay put,
and works at desktop and phone sizes alike.

The pinch is evened out where Chromium misses: one anchored near the top
does not zoom at all, so it starts lower, and one near the bottom
overshoots its ratio, so a small pinch from the middle corrects it. The
way out reads the real scale until the page is back at 1x, which the next
gesture needs.

The overlay also draws a fingertip per touch, so a pinch on a touch
device shows as two fingers.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: wait out a cold dev server before a demo starts

A fresh checkout's dev server optimizes its dependencies on the first
load and reloads the page, which can take well past an action's timeout,
so a demo failed before it started. The demo now waits up to 90 seconds
for the app; the recording only starts once it is ready.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: record a video per test in a PR demo, shown in a table

A large PR can split its demo into several shorter videos: each test()
in the ts demo block is recorded as its own video (<sha>-1.mp4, ...),
and the Demo section lays their previews out in a table, each column
headed by its test's title.

GIF previews now keep their longer side at DEMO_PREVIEW_WIDTH and shrink
until they are under 5 MB, since GitHub's image proxy refuses anything
larger and shows a broken image instead.

Importing traces works on a phone viewport too, where Settings sits in
the sidebar under the page until the menu key slides it aside.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: fix demo trace imports on desktop and lay landscape demos out two to a row

Importing traces failed on a desktop whose collapsed sidebar sits under
the page: it now expands the sidebar from the page's menu key on a phone
or from the sidebar's logo on a desktop, whichever makes Settings

commit.message:
qwen4exp: write the conv state tail without an intermediate cont (#31443)

build_conv_state_at makes a contiguous copy of the conv input tail
before writing it into the recurrent state, so every GDN layer issues
two device copies per generated token where one is enough. On
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (36 GDN layers) that is 72 copies per token, now 36.
Speculative decoding adds one more per rollback slot. ggml_cpy reads
the strided view directly, as the shared build_conv_state already does,
so the extra copy is dropped.

commit.message:
hexagon: faster TOP_K for the backend sampler (#31279)

* hexagon: faster TOP_K for the backend sampler (skip tiles, then block scan)

Skip the bitonic sort for tiles whose max cannot reach the running k-th
best value, then replace the tile sort with top_k_scan(): reject 256-float
blocks with one HVX max-reduce and insert only surviving elements into a
sorted k-entry list. Used for k in 2..64 and rows wider than 1024, in both
the single-row and multi-row paths.

Ties keep the first-seen index. NaN is treated as -INF.

* hex-top-k: eliminate scalar reads from vtcm

---------

Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky <maxk@qti.qualcomm.com>

commit.message:
gemma4: graph optimizations (massive gains on pp for E2B and E4B) (#31356)

* Optimizing Gemma4 graph for prompt processing

TODO:
	- Currently complete microbatch needs to contain tokens which does not require the logits; need to optimize this further
	- There are a few more operations that are performed after the kv cache is calculated, need to safely optimize them.

* Not filtering the rows when they are unmasked

* Cropping out the attention mask too.

* gemma-4: improved pruning, mask cropping and PLE scaling

Prune before the first KV-shared layer with the single-stream, causal, non-embedding safety gates.
Use cropped masks only during shared-layer attention.
Preserve requested layer-input embeddings in the KV prefix.
Remove the PLE contiguous materialization and fold equivalent PLE scaling into RMSNorm parameters/weights.

* spec-mtp: Enable masked h_nextn extraction only when the draft context shares the target KV cache

This lets Gemma 4 prune unused prompt rows before its shared layers so that we keep the full perf P.P gains with MTP.

Avoid extracting target hidden states for output-free prompt chunks in that shared-MTP path.
When a batch has a selected final token, extract only that row unless the whole verification batch is selected.

Keep ordinary MTP and classic speculative decoding behavior unchanged: they still use unmasked h_nextn because the draft
context must catch up on all target rows.

speculative-simple needs an update to select the final prompt row only for shared-KV MTP,
so the optimization works there without changing other speculative modes.
And it looks like the server already selects its final prompt row for first-token sampling.

* spec-mtp: make sure to not drop first draft round

* gemma4: enable pruning based on static cparams.kv_unified/n_seq_max=1

* gemma4-mtp: simplify prunning logic and avoid graph branches/re-allocs

* gemma4: update pruning gates to use only n_seq_max==1, kv_unified can now be used for multi-seq

* spec-simple: revert spec-simple changes for now

* gemma4: remove causal_attn from pruning gate (last source of reallocs)

* cont : adapt to llm_attn_mask changes

commit.message:
ggml : write host-buffer tensor data directly in gguf writer (#31144)

The gguf writer staged each tensor into a temporary vector before
writing it. For host-buffer tensors the data pointer is directly
writable, so skip the staging copy and write it straight to the file.
This avoids the per-tensor allocation, zero-init and memcpy.

commit.message:
ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach (#31584)

* ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach

A view was checked against its source with the size of a contiguous
tensor of the same shape, computed before its strides were set. Views
whose rows overlap failed that check although they stay inside their
source, and views with wider strides passed it while reaching past
the end. The view functions now pass their strides to the tensor
constructor, which checks the bytes they actually reach, like
ggml_nbytes. The conv windows of delta_net are created with all their
rows at once instead of being widened after the check.

* ggml: assert that a strided view starts from contiguous elements

The view functions set nb[0] to the type size, so the source must have
contiguous elements along dim 0 for the view to read them.

commit.message:
ggml : Gate RVV code on the target extension (#31607)

The RISC-V vector intrinsic specification requires __riscv_v_intrinsic
to be defined when the compiler supports the API, even when the vector
extension is not selected. Clang therefore defines it for rv64gc,
causing ggml to enter RVV branches where vector types are rejected
because the required ISA extensions are absent.

Use __riscv_v for optional RVV implementations; this macro represents
the selected target ISA. Retain __riscv_v_intrinsic checks in SpaceMIT
sources, where they validate mandatory compiler API support rather than
select optional vector code.

Closes: https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/issues/1535

commit.message:
gguf-py : validate every tokenizer merge pair, not only the first (#31631)

* gguf-py : validate every tokenizer merge pair, not only the first

The transformers 4.45 pair format was detected by checking merges[0],
then every element was converted unchecked: a non-pair element raised
a bare TypeError, and pairs with the wrong arity or non-string parts
were silently mangled into invalid merges.

Validate each element (2-string list) up front and raise the existing
"Unknown tokenizer merges format" error for anything else.

commit.message:
ui: open actions on right-click for chats, tabs, messages and models (#31545)

* ui : share directory resolution and the cwd row

Move the lookup of a browser-picked folder to ToolsService.resolveDirectoryPath, let the working directory picker run without its chip, and split the 'Set working directory to' row into its own component, so other views can pick and show a folder the same way.

Assisted by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui : open an item's actions on right-click

Sidebar conversations and models manager rows open the same actions as
their "more actions" menu on right-click. Both menus render one shared
list of actions, so they cannot drift apart. Phones keep the browser's
long-press; the dropdown's drawer already holds the actions there.
An action can render a flyout submenu in place of its row, through the
kit of the menu it is in, and close the menu after a pick.

Adds the shadcn-svelte context-menu component, mirroring the
dropdown-menu one.

Assisted by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui : close conversation tabs from a right-click menu

A tab's right-click menu closes it, the other tabs or the tabs to its
right, and stops a response the tab is generating. Closing tabs that
include the active one keeps the tab the menu was opened on.

Assisted by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui : open a message's actions on right-click

User and assistant messages open the same actions as their action icons
on right-click. Selected text, links, media, code and fields keep the
browser's own menu, so copying them works as before. The fork dialog
opens from the actions context, like the delete one, so both the icon
and the menu can open it.

Assisted by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui : scope right-click menu shortcuts and selection to their item

Show the conversation shortcuts only on the active row, as they act on
the active conversation, and keep the browser menu only for a selection
inside the message. Name the close-tab shortcut, and drop the unused
chip toggle, menu submenus and shared cwd row.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

commit.message:
llama : fix on-device state copy sizes for quantized KV caches (#30541)

* llama : fix on-device state copy sizes for quantized KV caches

The on-device sequence state copies (LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE) computed
their element count as size / ggml_element_size(). For a quantized type such as
q8_0 or q4_0 that is the number of blocks, not elements, so only part of each
range was copied: the restored state was wrong, or the copy crashed.

Compute the count as size / ggml_type_size() * ggml_blck_size() for the save,
the restore and the copy between differently chunked ranges, and assert that
each range covers whole blocks.

* llama : drop the one-line comments

* llama : drop the redundant cast in the state copy size

* llama : fix on-device state copy sizes for quantized KV caches

The on-device sequence state copies (LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE) computed
their element count as size / ggml_element_size(). For a quantized type such as
q8_0 or q4_0 that is the number of blocks, not elements, so only part of each
range was copied: the restored state was wrong, or the copy crashed.

Compute the count as size / ggml_type_size() * ggml_blck_size() for the save,
the restore and the copy between differently chunked ranges, and assert that
each range covers whole blocks.

commit.message:
metal: keep fusable node groups inside one command buffer (#31688)

The first command buffer takes the first 10% of the graph nodes and the
rest is split evenly between the extra command buffers. A fusion cannot
span two command buffers, so a boundary that falls inside a fusable
group runs that group unfused, and the output then depends on the node
count of the graph.

Move each boundary to the end of the fusable group it falls into, so
the encoders fuse the same nodes as with a single command buffer.

commit.message:
tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties (#31426)

* tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties

With uniform random logits, two experts sometimes land within one f32
ulp of each other at a routing boundary, mostly with sqrt_softplus
gating whose output range is narrow. A backend whose gating differs by
a few ulps from the CPU then picks the other expert and the test fails.

Draw each row of logits again until the group selection and the final
top-k both have a relative margin of 1e-4, computed on the host in
double precision.

* tests: build the TOPK_MOE logits by inverting the gating function

Draw the selection scores (probs plus bias) of each row as a random
permutation of a grid, move the experts of the best groups up by half a
step, and set the logits to the inverse of the gating function at these
scores. Every expert and group decision is then one grid step apart on
all backends, and the host no longer recomputes the routing.

The softmax probs are built to sum to one so that the softmax keeps the
scores, and the views of the logits are not initialized again after the
logits are set.

commit.message:
graph: store the MTP conv snapshots of every recurrent model in one set_rows (#31660)

* graph: store the conv state of every rollback arch in one set_rows

The rollback slots of the causal conv history were written with one
copy per slot in qwen4exp, glm5-next, kimi-k3, bailingmoe3, lfm and
mamba2, while delta_net already wrote them with a single set_rows.
build_conv_state_store now does this for all of them: one copy without
rollback, otherwise one set_rows of the overlapping windows into the
min(n, n_rs_seq + 1) slots a rollback can read.

The slot order {n_rs_seq, ..., 0} is computed once per graph and each
conv layer takes a view of its tail. Its size does not depend on the
ubatch, so the reserved graph covers every ubatch shape, and the graph
input that held it is gone.

A model that is not causal never rolls back, so the context clamps
n_rs_seq to 0 for it, like for an arch without rollback support.

* nits: compute the conv slot order in the graph and keep the n_head name of bailingmoe3

* graph: build the conv slot order in each conv layer

The slot order {K-1, ..., 0} of the conv state store was one tensor
shared by every conv layer of the graph, built on the device of the
first one, so each layer on another device copied the view of its
tail. Each conv layer now builds its own order next to its set_rows,
and llm_graph_input_rs no longer holds it.

commit.message:
fit : account for skipped NextN layers when setting n_gpu_layers (#31569)

* fit : account for skipped NextN layers when setting n_gpu_layers

Without MTP, fit counts n_layer + 1 layers while the model loader counts
n_layer_all + 1 for n_gpu_layers, including the NextN layers which hold no
weights. A fit result that offloads all layers then leaves layer 0 on the CPU
("offloaded 65/66 layers" for Qwen3.8-27B on two GPUs).

Add the skipped NextN layers to n_gpu_layers and to the tensor split of the
device that holds the output layer so the loader assigns the layers that
fit measured.

Fixes #31531

* fit : pass hp_ngl_skip by reference like the other hparams

* fit : add hp_ngl_skip to common_get_device_memory_data

commit.message:
conversion : resolve quantized_layers from source tensor names (#31611)

* conversion : resolve quantized_layers from source tensor names

This commit changes how the per layer NVFP4 quant_algo are resolved from
hf_quant_config.json quantized_layers.

The keys in quantized_layers are module paths in the source checkpoint,
and these can be either be modules like 'lm_head' or parent modules
like 'layers.0.ffn.experts'. Currently these keys are passed through
filter_tensors, but they are not tensor names. So a filter_tensors that
keeps an explicit list of tensor names, like Nemotron's with --mtp
would drop them. That means there was no `_nvfp4_layer_algo entry`, and
`_tag_prec_a4` fell back to `_nvfp4_global_algo`.

This commit records the mapping from source tensor name to filtered
tensor name in index_tensors. Then in prepare_tensors each source
tensor is resolved to its closest quantized_layers parent, and
the algo is stored under the filtered tensor name, which is what
_tag_prec_a4 later looks up.

Converting Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 with --mtp now produces:
```console
    general.tensor_extra.name = ['output.weight']
    general.tensor_extra.prec_a4 = [False]
```
whereas on master no general.tensor_extra fields are written. For the
non-MTP conversion, the general.tensor_extra fields are identical to
master.

Also manually verified (using pdb) that this works for
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-NVFP4.

Refs: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31602#issuecomment-6603337403

* conversion : shorten comment

* conversion : also remove '.bias' suffixes

commit.message:
ggml : support `truncate=false` for YaRN (#30206)

* ggml : support `truncate=false` for YaRN

YaRN calculates correction intervals to switch frequency interpolation
methods, but the setting to not round the boundaries of these intervals
to integers (`truncate=false`) was not supported.

Models that use `truncate=false` include gpt-oss and some PLaMo-3
models; to support them correctly, the GGML operations and CPU backend
are modified to handle calculations without rounding. The default
behavior is `truncate=true`, and existing calls not explicitly
configured will maintain their previous behavior.

* support CUDA backend

* add tests

* move RoPE helpers to internal header

* format

commit.message:
vulkan: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (#29772)

* vulkan: add F16 input to the FWHT

The Vulkan FWHT accepts F32 input only. This adds an F16 source variant of the
shader, for both the subgroup and the shared-memory paths, so the kernel reads
an F16 source directly instead of requiring a converted copy.

The F16 shader needs shader-float16, so the pipelines are only created when the
device reports it. A null pipeline makes ggml_vk_can_use_fwht fall back, which
is the same path an unsupported width already takes.

supports_op and the dispatch both already route through ggml_vk_can_use_fwht,
so there is a single place asking whether an op qualifies; nothing to
consolidate here the way the CUDA/Metal ports needed.

test-backend-ops on an M5 Pro (MoltenVK, fp16: 1): MUL_MAT 1128/1128,
including all 24 Hadamard cases (18 existing F32, 6 new F16).

Assisted-by: Codex

* vulkan: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512

The Vulkan FWHT covers block widths 64 to 512; wider blocks fall back to the
dense matmul. Extend the width list to 8192 and pick the shader per width: the
subgroup shader keeps n/subgroup_size values per invocation, so widths above
512 (or a subgroup narrow enough to exceed 64 values per invocation) use the
shared-memory shader with one row per workgroup and a 256-wide block. The rows
per workgroup become a specialization constant so the dispatch matches.

Pipelines for a width are only created when the device's shared-memory and
workgroup-invocation limits allow it; otherwise that width keeps the fallback.

This is the Vulkan counterpart to #29100 (CUDA). Stacked on #29101; the last
commit is the one to review.

Assisted-by: Codex

commit.message:
metal : fuse DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and GLM MoE routing (#31615)

* metal : support scale-bias routing norm in the TOPK_MOE fusion

The DeepSeek-V4.1 graph normalizes the routing weights with a scale+bias
(sum + 1e-20) instead of the lower clamp used by the other models. Add
norm_bias/norm_scale_bias fusion chains that accept a SCALE node with a
unit scale factor at the clamp position, pass an additive bias in the
kernel args, and apply it as max(wt_sum, clamp) + bias so both variants
share one kernel. Cover the new chains in test-backend-ops.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* metal : fuse sqrt(softplus) MoE routing with a selection bias

Add TOPK_MOE chains anchored at the softplus node (UNARY+SQRT+ADD+
ARGSORT+GET_ROWS plus optional norm/scale) so the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1
routing fuses on Metal. The kernel scores with sqrt(softplus) and ranks
selection-biased keys while the gathered weights and the norm stay
unbiased, matching the reference graph. Dispatch hooks at the softplus
node, cover the norm-bias combination in test-backend-ops and record the
new deepseek4/deepseek41 fusion counters.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* metal : fuse sigmoid MoE routing with a selection bias

The sigmoid-gated MoE archs (GLM, DeepSeek-V2/V3.2, ...) rank
sigmoid(logits) + exp_probs_b with an optional weights-norm, but only
the softmax and sqrt(softplus) routing chains were fusable.

- add 6 sigmoid-anchored TOPK_MOE chains: sigmoid + ADD + ARGSORT +
  GET_ROWS with optional SCALE and SUM_ROWS + CLAMP/SCALE + DIV norm
  tail; the selection-bias ADD is required, same as the sqrt(softplus)
  chains
- generalize the gating function constant from a sqrt(softplus) bool
  to an int (0 = softmax, 1 = sqrt(softplus), 2 = sigmoid); sigmoid
  scores are 1 / (1 + exp(-logits)), matching the CPU, Metal unary and
  CUDA kernels
- anchor the unary dispatch hook at sigmoid nodes too
- test-backend-ops: 4 sigmoid routing cases with and without a
  weights scale
- re-record tests/fusion/MTL.csv: the sigmoid archs (glm5-next,
  deepseek2/32, kimi, minimax, ...) now fuse their routing, and
  muse-spark prefill drops one MOE_REDUCE fire because the reordered
  graph allocates the routing weights inside the reduce output range,
  which the dst/input overlap check correctly declines

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* cont : remove low-signal comments

* ocd : valign ggml_metal_fusions

commit.message:
model : add Ripple (ricursiveai) (#31692)

* feat : added ricursiveai ripple support

* fix : mandatiry SWA, scale through helper, comments back

* fix : metal

* model : make ricursive RoPE/NoPE explicit and validate the layer pattern

Write attention.rope_pattern and read it as optional, falling back to the
sliding window pattern so existing GGUFs keep loading. Refuse a
sliding_window_pattern that does not cover every layer, a model with no
sliding layer, and a gate or value residual present in only some layers.
The converter derives layer_types when the config omits it, ignores a stale
hybrid_layer_pattern and drops tensors of features the config disables.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* model : make ricursive swiglu_clamp per-layer

Store swiglu_clamp as a per-layer array, read it with get_key_or_arr so the
scalar in existing GGUFs still applies to every layer, and refuse a negative
or non-finite value. Add a test-llama-archs fixture with mixed per-layer
clamps and no rope_pattern, so the saver roundtrip checks both.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* model : use the ricursive per-tensor scales and RoPE parameters

Pass the attn_gate and output weight scales to build_lora_mm, take
ext_factor and attn_factor from the graph instead of hardcoding them, and
copy rope_freq_scale_train to the SWA layers instead of pinning it to 1.
Cite the reference lines for the value residual and the NoPE layers.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* convert : drop the ricursive chat_template.jinja override

The precedence between tokenizer_config.json and chat_template.jinja is to
be changed in SpecialVocab for all models instead. Until then a new
conversion stores the short tokenizer_config.json template; GGUFs that
already carry the tool-aware template are not affected.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

* fix : remove NVFP4 checkpoint quantization block

* match #31733 refactor

---------

commit.message:
tests : override hardware_concurrency in CI (#31797)

The self-hosted CPU runners are containers with 8 CPUs, but
std::thread::hardware_concurrency reports the cores of the host. The
table mode of test-llama-context sizes its pool from that count, so it
runs 4 models x 8 threads on an 8-CPU job and hangs.

Add TEST_ARG_HARDWARE_CONCURRENCY and TEST_ARG_PARALLEL_WORKERS as the
defaults for the auto-selected counts of test-llama-context and of
test-backend-ops, and set them to 8 and 4 for cpu-x64-high-perf.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

commit.message:
tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std:: (#31791)

* tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std::

The unqualified calls rely on the C math.h names also being present in the
global namespace, which is not the case for the NetBSD 11.99.9/x86_64 gcc
14.4.0 build reported in the issue.  Prefix the calls with std:: to select
the standard C++ overloads declared by <cmath>.

ref: https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/issues/1681

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB)

* tests : qualify C math calls with std::

Follow-up to the isnan / signbit fix: make the remaining math calls in
test-quantize-fns.cpp consistent with the std:: isfinite / max / numeric_limits
already used in the same file.

The float variants are overloads in C++, not distinct names, so the mapping is
fabsf -> std::fabs, copysignf -> std::copysign, nextafterf -> std::nextafter -
not std::fabsf & friends, which do not exist in libstdc++ and would break the
gcc build.  NAN and INFINITY are macros and are left unqualified.

Only behavioural difference: array_rmse() fed a double accumulator to sqrtf(),
now std::sqrt() keeps the computation in double.  The result is more accurate
and differs from the previous value by at most 1.4e-7 relative, three orders of
magnitude below the tightest tolerance in this test.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB)

+name: Behavior Check
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch: # allows manual triggering
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - master
+    paths: [
+      '.github/workflows/behavior-check.yml',
+      '**/CMakeLists.txt',
+      '**/.cmake',
+      '**/*.h',
+      '**/*.hpp',
+      '**/*.c',
+      '**/*.cpp',
+      '**/*.py',
+      '**/requirements*.txt',
+    ]
+
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths: [
+      '.github/workflows/behavior-check.yml',
+      '**/CMakeLists.txt',
+      '**/.cmake',
+      '**/*.h',
+      '**/*.hpp',
+      '**/*.c',
+      '**/*.cpp',
+      '**/*.py',
+      '**/requirements*.txt',
+    ]
+
+cache-mode: none
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref && github.ref || github.run_id }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+env:
+  GGML_NLOOP: 3
+  GGML_N_THREADS: 1
+  GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC: 1
+  LLAMA_ARG_LOG_COLORS: 1
+  LLAMA_ARG_LOG_PREFIX: 1
+  LLAMA_ARG_LOG_TIMESTAMPS: 1
+
+jobs:
+  ubuntu:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04-arm
+
+    steps:
+      - name: Clone
+        id: checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: ccache
+        uses: ggml-org/ccache-action@v1.2.24
+        with:
+          restore: false
+          save: false
+
+      - name: Build Dependencies
+        id: build_depends
+        run: |
+          sudo apt update
+          sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev git-lfs libjpeg-dev python3 python3-venv python3-pip
+
+      - name: Python Dependencies
+        id: python_depends
+        run: |
+          python3 -m venv .venv
+          source .venv/bin/activate
+          pip install -r requirements/requirements-convert_hf_to_gguf.txt
+
+      - name: ccache-buckets-restore
+        uses: ./.github/actions/ccache-buckets
+        env:
+          HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN_CI }}
+        with:
+          key: behavior-check-ubuntu-26.04-arm
+          folder: llama.cpp
+          hf_bucket: ggml-org/cache
+
+      - name: Build
+        id: cmake_build
+        run: |
+          cmake -B build \
+            -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
+            -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=OFF \
+            -DLLAMA_FATAL_WARNINGS=ON
+          time cmake --build build --config Release -j $(nproc)
+
+      - name: ccache-buckets-save
+        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
+        uses: ./.github/actions/ccache-buckets
+        env:
+          HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN_CACHE_OUTPUT }}
+        with:
+          key: behavior-check-ubuntu-26.04-arm
+          folder: llama.cpp
+          evict-old-files: 1d
+          hf_bucket: ggml-org/cache
+          save: true
+
+      - name: Test
+        id: cmake_test
+        run: |
+          source .venv/bin/activate
+          cd build
+          ctest -L behavior -LE 'model|backend' --verbose --timeout 900
+
+  windows:
+    runs-on: windows-2025
+
+    cache-mode: write
+    permissions:
+      actions: write
+      contents: read
+
+    steps:
+      - name: Clone
+        id: checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: ccache
+        uses: ggml-org/ccache-action@v1.2.24
+        with:
+          key: behavior-check-windows-2025
+          evict-old-files: 1d
+          save: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
+
+      - name: Python Dependencies
+        id: python_depends
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          python3 -m venv .venv
+          source .venv/Scripts/activate
+          pip install -r requirements/requirements-convert_hf_to_gguf.txt
+
+      - name: Build
+        id: cmake_build
+        shell: cmd
+        run: |
+          call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Enterprise\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64
+          cmake -B build -G "Ninja Multi-Config" ^
+            -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/x64-windows-llvm.cmake ^
+            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ^
+            -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF ^
+            -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=OFF
+          set /A NINJA_JOBS=%NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS%-1
+          cmake --build build --config Release -j %NINJA_JOBS%
+
+      - name: Test
+        id: cmake_test
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          source .venv/Scripts/activate
+          cd build
+          ctest -C Release -L behavior -LE 'model|backend' --verbose --timeout 900
+
+      - name: ccache-clear
+        uses: ./.github/actions/ccache-clear
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        with:
+          key: behavior-check-windows-2025
+          older: 5m
+          min: 1
+          dry-run: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || github.ref != 'refs/heads/master' }}
